A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MixMin work. All 17 pages, including Appendix A proofs and Appendix B tables and figures, support reliable comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: v2 reports original language-model pretraining and PCBA bioassay experiments, including baseline comparisons, compute analyses and model-scale transfer results in Section 6 and Appendix B.

after.justification: v3 retains these original language-model and bioassay experiments and their reported outcomes in Section 6 and Appendix B.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects the loss prefactor from lambda_p/|D_t| to 1/|D_t| and changes both update exponents from +eta*g_p to -eta*g_p. These localized corrections make the pseudocode implement the minimization already described in Section 4; they do not establish a changed experimental implementation.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama sources with PIQA, ARC-Easy, SciQ and OpenWebMath targets, plus the same PCBA bioassay coverage. No datasets, tasks or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: Natural and balanced mixtures, random search and RegMix retain their membership in the corresponding comparisons. Appendix B also preserves the same chemistry baseline comparisons and their restricted coverage at the largest source count.

E3.justification: The language-model 80/20 splits, 160M/410M models and 3.2B/8.2B-token budgets remain unchanged. Chemistry retains its 64/16/20 split, preprocessing and tuning procedures. Evaluation metrics and controls are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The compute-budget sensitivity, model-scale transfer, source-count, retraining-versus-ensembling, assay-weight and cross-task analyses are retained without changes in their questions or evidence, including Appendix B.

E5.justification: Both versions retain three-trial reporting with 95% confidence intervals, Welch's t-tests in Tables 3–5, and the separate five-trial PIQA results in Figure 18. No run-count or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: Performance plots, assay rankings, mixture weights and p-values match throughout Section 6 and Appendix B, including Figure 18. The pseudocode corrections are not accompanied by revised scores or findings.

T1.justification: The formal objectives, Theorem 3.1, Lemma 3.2, assumptions, bounds and Appendix A proofs are unchanged. Appendix A.2 is relabeled 'Theorem 3.2' without changing its mathematics; Algorithm 1 is corrected to match the existing objective.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims about convex reduction, cheap proxy models, baseline improvements and robustness to reduced proxy compute.

C2.justification: Interpretations of weak proxies, scale transfer and selected assay sources are unchanged. The limitations concerning CE/MSE, covariate shift, image classification and proxy-model quality are retained.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures remain unchanged, including eta=1 for 100 MixMin steps, proxy-training budgets, A100/AMD EPYC hardware, XGBoost hyperparameters and code/data access links.

R1.justification: The cited works, reference list and Section 5 positioning relative to RegMix, other data-mixing methods and bilevel optimization approaches remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The author name changes from 'Yangjuan Ruan' to 'Yangjun Ruan', and Appendix A.2 changes 'Lemma 3.2' to 'Theorem 3.2', although Section 3.2 still labels it a lemma. The prose and section organization otherwise remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The same 18 figures, five tables and algorithm box retain their designs, captions, ordering and placement. The algorithm's formula corrections do not introduce a display redesign or document-layout restructuring.

improvement.justification: v3 removes the extraneous loss factor and reverses the erroneous gradient sign in Algorithm 1, making the pseudocode consistent with Section 4 and more reliable to implement. The underlying theory and empirical evidence remain unchanged. Appendix A.2 introduces a small lemma/theorem labeling inconsistency, but the algorithm corrections provide a clear, limited net improvement.
